analysis.investment_thesis: FACT fails both Magic Formula tests catastrophically: Earnings Yield is ~0.16% (EBIT ₹95 Cr / EV ~₹60,011 Cr) against my required threshold of >12%, and ROIC is roughly 1-2% against my required >20%. At a P/E of 3,944x and EV/EBITDA of 136.5x, the market is paying an absurd premium for a business that barely earns anything.
key_strengths: 90% government promoter backing provides implicit sovereign support and subsidy access
Revenue CAGR of 9.8% over 9 years shows scale growth, though not quality growth
OCF positive all 5 of the last 5 years — company does generate some operating cash
key_risks: Earnings yield near zero (~0.16%) — stock is priced as if it earns 600x more than it does
Operating margin is NEGATIVE at -3.28%; operating income of ₹95 Cr is a rounding error on ₹4,051 Cr revenue
Borrowings spiked from ₹1,810 Cr (2024) to ₹3,837 Cr (2025) — a 2x debt increase in one year with deteriorating earnings
red_flags: P/E of 3,944x — virtually all 'earnings' are non-operating Other Income (₹241 Cr vs Net Profit ₹41 Cr in 2025)
Net profit collapsing: ₹613 Cr (2023) → ₹128 Cr (2024) → ₹41 Cr (2025) — 93% decline in 2 years
FCF turned negative in 2025 (-₹13 Cr) for the first time
ROCE of 8.65% barely covers cost of debt — no economic value creation
Profit history is lumpy and subsidy-driven: Other Income swings wildly (₹1,004 Cr in 2020, -₹42 Cr in 2024, ₹241 Cr in 2025)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying the Magic Formula, FACT is one of the worst-scoring stocks I can imagine. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) = ₹95 Cr / ~₹60,011 Cr ≈ 0.16%, roughly 75x below my 12% threshold. Return on Capital is equally dismal — with EBIT of ₹95 Cr on an asset base exceeding ₹6,677 Cr, ROIC is in the low single digits. The reported ROCE of 8.65% understates the problem since much of the profit is from volatile government subsidies and "Other Income," not core operations. The operating margin of -3.28% means the fertilizer business itself is loss-making at the operating level.

The stock's valuation (P/E 3,944x, EV/EBITDA 136.5x, P/S 25x) is the result of PSU-driven market speculation, not fundamentals. This is a government-owned fertilizer company with Debt/Equity of 2.79, borrowings that doubled in FY2025, and a net profit that has collapsed 93% from its peak. The Magic Formula explicitly rejects businesses like this — no sustainable earnings yield, no return on capital, high capital intensity, and profits driven by one-time government transfers rather than durable competitive advantage. There is no price at which a deteriorating PSU with near-zero ROIC and negative operating margins qualifies as a "good business bought cheap."
